business_scope.primary_industry_name: Off-Price Wholesale Liquidation of Branded Overstock Apparel

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America (KORUS FTA, 2012)
Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the European Union and its Member States (Korea-EU FTA, 2011)
Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (Korea-China BIT, 2007)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transactions Reports Act (Act No. 6516), as amended, and its Presidential Enforcement Decree No. 24535; the Real Name Financial Transactions Act (Act No. 4678); and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) Beneficial Ownership Information Reporting Notice (2024-1), together establishing the legal basis for customer due diligence and UBO disclosure obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Registration (Certificate of Registered Matters) for the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Administrative Office of the Republic of Korea (District Court Registration Bureau, place of incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the Korean court registry; authenticated by a notary public if executed in Korea, then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea under the Hague Apostille Convention; no consular legalization by an embassy or consulate of Korea shall be chained or added; for a foreign-origin exhibit, the competent authority of the State of origin issues the apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance Certificate / No Outstanding Corporate Tax)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (or District Tax Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route only: issued by the National Tax Service, followed by apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Korea; consular legalization is not applicable because the Republic of Korea is a Party to the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation and appointment of representative director, or Power of Attorney granted to the local incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign parent/shareholder (or the sole corporate member) plus a notary public in Korea if notarization is required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The resolution/PoA is executed in the country of origin, notarized by a local notary, and then apostilled by the competent authority in the origin State; if executed in Korea, apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular legalization is not permitted to be stacked after an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Bylaws of the Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators / subscribers, executed and notarized before a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in Korea and, where required for international transaction purposes, apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the Hague Convention; no consular legalization route may be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Corporate Bank Reference / AML KYC introduction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Fiscal agent or corporate bank where the shareholder or related entity maintains an account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter is issued on bank letterhead, notarized if required, then apostilled by the competent authority of the issuing state; for states that are Party to the Apostille Convention, apostille only; for non-member states, consular legalization would be required instead, but these two methods are parallel and mutually exclusive and never combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: PEP and sanctions screening must be conducted against every individual beneficial owner, director, authorized signatory, and correspondent bank through automated and manual checks using the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's domestic watchlist, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated targets, and Interpol notices. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for foreign senior officials, their family and close associates. Hit resolution requires documented rationale, adverse media review, and escalation to the AML compliance officer before any name clearance or banking introduction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (Government e-Court Commercial Registration Database)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act and Registration of Commerce Act, the legal form must be shown as 'Yuhan Hoesa' (limited liability company) in the Korean trade name. The trade name must be written in Korean script; a transliterated English name may be recorded as a concurrent trading name if it does not create confusion with existing registered names. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive main element, (2) the business purpose word or industry identifier, (3) a geographical or branch qualifier if desired, and (4) the mandatory legal form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' or its English equivalent '(Co., Ltd.)'. Phonetic transliteration must follow the Korean Government's standard Romanization rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant may first correct obvious conflicts by filing a new application through the same e-Court portal. A written administrative appeal must be filed with the competent District Court Registration Office within 14 days from receipt of the rejection notice, stating the grounds of distinguishability, including evidence that no identical or confusingly similar registered trade name exists in the same business classification. The applicant may attach prior registrations, trademark certificates, or court decisions. A further corrective petition to the Supreme Court or an administrative review before the relevant administrative agency is available only after an initial ruling. Legal counsel involvement is strongly advised; appeals are processed within 20 business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a low-risk off-price apparel wholesale liquidation company, a virtual office or commercial mailbox may be acceptable for the initial corporate registry filing, but the local district tax office and major commercial banks generally require a physical place of business that is accessible for document service, VAT invoice registration, and inspections. A virtual office will be rejected for bank account opening if it is not a registered business hotel or serviced office provider that can produce a lease contract and a registered address proof. The National Tax Service treats virtual-only addresses as an indicator for amplified due diligence and may deny a business registration number for the wholesale trade sector if no actual storage, sales or administrative facility exists. Accordingly, virtual office use is possible only in narrow circumstances with a licensed business center that offers a dedicated office lease, mail handling, and meeting facilities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) existence of a physical lease or ownership deed for the registered office; (2) presence of at least one employee during business hours; (3) availability of corporate books, VAT invoices, and customs/trade documentation on site; (4) display or external identification of the registered business name; (5) consistency between the address on tax invoices, bank statements, and customs declarations. Quantified risk: for a low-risk wholesale trader, the probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by a municipal tax office or registry official within the first year is approximately 15-25%; the risk increases to 40-50% if the registered address is a virtual office or a mail-drop center, or if the entity is linked to a high-volume cash or chargeback pattern.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government commercial registration fee and court filing fee for the incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea, District Court Registration Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Commercial Act and Court Fees Act; registration fee is calculated on stated capital (0.4%, subject to a floor) plus a fixed education surcharge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate legal fee for drafting Articles of Association, shareholder resolution, and incorporation advisory
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean law firm (fee paid to attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for fixed-fee LLC incorporations in Seoul (USD 1,000 to 1,500), reflecting senior associate time.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search and availability report through the corporate registry database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office / authorized corporate service agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official portal search fee (USD 2-5) plus corporate secretarial service fee at market rate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization fee for Articles of Association and certified copies of incorporation instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean notary public (appointed by the Ministry of Justice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prescribed tariff under the Notary Public Act; typical charge for certified notarial act ranges from USD 50-150 depending on page count.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and legalization processing (Hague apostille, domestic and foreign origin documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea / competent authority in the origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government apostille fee (typically USD 20-60 per document) plus courier/translation coordination service charge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter procurement and AML KYC onboarding package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean commercial bank (beneficiary account institution) and corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariffs for corporate account KYC and reference letter issuance (USD 50-150) plus outsourced compliance support.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (as amended), Articles 543 through 595 governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited company); Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 5 and 6, if non-resident members subscribe; the Commercial Registration Act and its Enforcement Decree as the procedural registration law; the Electronic Registration Act for online filing through the IROS portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Bureau, Supreme Court of Korea, through the Internet Registration System (IROS) at www.iros.go.kr; substantive filing is made with the competent District Court Registry Office in the jurisdiction of the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration under the Commercial Registration Act, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan), the capital payment certificate, evidence of consent of all founding members, and the corporate registration tax payment confirmation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose any statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa and there is no blocked escrow account requirement. The members may fix the initial capital freely in the Articles of Incorporation, but the subscribed capital must be paid in full before the incorporation registration application is filed, and a bank-issued payment certificate must be submitted to the registry. If foreign investment is involved, the remitted capital must be received through a designated foreign-exchange bank and reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolution No. 2025-KYH-001 of the First Meeting of the Board of Directors and Founding Members of KR Yuhan Hoesa, a limited company formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, lawfully called and convened at the registered office in Seoul, Republic of Korea, on the date of incorporation. The chairperson confirmed that notice was duly given or waived, that a quorum was present throughout, and that each participant had full legal capacity. After discussion, the following binding resolutions were adopted by unanimous consent. Section 1. Share Capital Subscription. The board adopts the authenticated and notarized Articles of Incorporation, fixing the total contributed capital at the amount stated therein, and approves the member quota ledger signed by each founding member. Each member has irrevocably subscribed to the allocated quota and has paid the contribution in full into the pre-incorporation temporary subscription account. The representative director is authorized to acknowledge the receipt of capital, issue contribution certificates, and transfer all paid-in capital to the corporate account after registration. No reduction or redemption of capital may be effected prior to statutory creditor protection procedures. Section 2. Banking Authorization. The board designates the bank and branch set out in the minutes as the corporate depositary for the Company. The representative director and the compliance officer are jointly and severally authorized, acting through dual signatures, to open, maintain, close and operate all current and savings accounts, to issue, sign and endorse cheques, bills, receipts and payment orders, and to transmit settlement instructions by SWIFT wire or ACH rails for the purchase and liquidation of finished garment inventories. All electronic banking mandates shall be preserved in the corporate records. Section 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company is fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, within the jurisdiction of the competent District Court Registry. The representative director is authorized to execute and deliver the office lease, utility agreements and related facility contracts, and to notify the registry of any subsequent change of the registered office in the manner required by law. Section 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following founding officers are appointed to their respective statutory offices: representative director, director and auditor, and compliance officer. Each appointee accepts the fiduciary duties and discretionary powers assigned by the Commercial Act, the Articles of Incorporation and these minutes. The officers are directed to cause the Company to obtain its business registration certificate, to complete customs and warehousing permits if inventory physically crosses borders or is stored, to procure civil defense and fire safety clearances for any storage premises, and to institute internal controls for the low-risk wholesale payments profile. This resolution is a final and binding corporate act and may be relied upon by all government authorities, financial institutions and counterparties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Articles of Incorporation and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: IROS Electronic Registration Portal of the Supreme Court; a notary public under the Notary Act of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search for the intended corporate name through IROS. If the name is available, prepare Korean-language Articles of Incorporation specifying the exact name of the Company, the registered office address, the total amount of contributed capital, the member quotas, the business purpose covering wholesale trade in finished garments under ISIC 4641 and liquidation of branded overstock apparel, and the first statutory officers. The Articles of Incorporation must be executed by all founding members in person or by a notarized and apostilled power of attorney. Present the capacity of the subscribing members, confirm absence of an unlawful purpose and proceed to notarization. The notarized instrument serves as the foundation for all subsequent registration and licensing steps and must reflect the isolation of liabilities and banking authorities.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all founding members
Apostilled or legalized power of attorney if representation is used
Draft corporate minutes of the inaugural meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court or notary queries any article, correct the provision and resubmit without prejudice. If IROS returns the name as unavailable, apply with a new secondary name and priority date. If the notarial certificate is defective, reexecute the Articles before the notary public within seven business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent District Court Registry Office in the jurisdiction of the registered office, via the IROS internet registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of notarization and after all subscriptions have been paid, file the Application for Incorporation Registration with the court registry. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank-issued capital payment certificate, the minutes appointing officers, the written consent of each officer to serve in office, and the power of attorney appointing a local agent if the application is filed remotely. The registry will verify the capital payment, the legality of the stated business purpose, the officer identities and the registered office documentation. Once satisfied, the registry assigns a company registration number, records the initial capital and issues the official Corporate Registration Certificate, thereby conferring separate legal personality. This certificate must match the exact corporate name and task identifier for subsequent tax and licensing files.
required_dossiers: Consent to office executed by each statutory officer
Power of attorney for the local filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, supply the supplementary document within the court-granted period. If registration is refused, submit a written legal opinion and corrected application within two weeks, or appeal to the higher court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Value Added Tax Enrollment with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through its Hometax online portal at www.hometax.go.kr; the competent District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After legal personality is established, the representative director must submit the Business Registration Application by the statutory deadline. The application must select the proper industry classification codes ISIC 4641 and NAICS 424320 and describe the activity as off-price whole-sale liquidation of branded overstock finished garments. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate, which is mandatory for issuing electronic tax invoices, obtaining corporate tax identification and enrolling for VAT. In the same process the Company should register for the national e-invoice system and open the electronic tax mail account. If the Company will clear apparel through customs, the compliance officer must also register the Company as an importer and exporter with the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS portal.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the representative director
Lease agreement or ownership proof for the registered office
Business activity declaration with ISIC 4641 and NAICS 424320
If applicable, foreign investment report receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Hometax rejects or delays the business registration, correct the classification code, adjust the lease submission and resubmit within five business days. A refusal order may be appealed internally to the National Tax Service under its protest and adjudication procedure. Any late registration will be regularized by filing a late return with a written explanation and paying the applicable penalty according to the tax due day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Capital Release
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank headquartered in Korea, principally at the branch nearest the registered office; the bank acts under the Financial Services Commission AML/CFT supervision.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director and compliance officer must open the permanent corporate account in the exact legal name of KR Yuhan Hoesa. The bank will apply customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership verification in line with the low-risk standard of the business. Present the Corporate Registration Certificate, Business Registration Certificate, notarized Articles, signatory appointments and identification documents. The bank will release the pre-incorporation subscription funds into the main corporate account and issue the final capital payment certificate. If foreign capital has been subscribed, the foreign investor must file the foreign investment report with the designated bank before the capital is credited, and the bank will verify the remittance under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The bank also enrolls the Company for SWIFT wire and ACH direct payment services.
required_dossiers: Board resolution or minutes approving the bank and authorized signatories
Identity documents and proof of address of directors
Business profile and financial information form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide the requested source-of-funds evidence and ownership transparency within seven business days. If the application is refused, resubmit at another licensed bank with the complete dossier or seek a remedy through the financial institution complaint process supervised by the Financial Supervisory Service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Officer Registers, Social Insurance and Post-Incorporation Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service, Ministry of Employment and Labor, and local fire authority in the district of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The compliance officer should update the statutory corporate registers, including the member register, the quota register and the register of directors and auditors, and retain the notarized Articles and all integer minutes in the minute book. Within the statutory employment period, the Company must file the insurance scheme enrollment applications for employment insurance, national pension, national health insurance and long-term care insurance through the integrated social insurance portal. For the physical warehouse supporting garment liquidation, appoint a workplace safety manager and apply for the fire facilities completion inspection before occupancy if the premises receive, sort or dispatch inventory. These steps ensure that the Company operates lawfully under Korean employment, health, safety and fire codes.
required_dossiers: Employer enrollment forms for the four social insurance schemes
Appointment letter for workplace safety manager
Warehouse lease and fire inspection drawings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an employment insurance or social insurance filing is accepted late, submit the overdue return with mitigating circumstances and request a penalty waiver. If fire inspection fails, remedy the fire safety deficiencies and request a re-inspection within 30 days. If the labor inspection finds non-compliance, implement the corrective order and submit written evidence of rectification to the Ministry of Employment and Labor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Korea Customs Service for customs registration and cross-border apparel clearance; competent District Tax Office and local Gu office for general wholesale trade business registration; National Fire Agency for fire and civil defense clearance of exhibition, storage and dispatch facilities; Ministry of Environment for any environmental assessment that may apply to a large distribution warehouse.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration Certificate for General Wholesale Trade of Finished Garments; Import/Export Registration Certificate under the Korea Customs Service; Fire-Fighting System Completion Inspection Certificate for any warehouse ancillary to the off-price liquidation distribution activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Environmental Impact Assessment Bureau, together with the local environmental regulatory branch having jurisdiction over the warehouse site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment for the pure wholesale and liquidation trade of finished apparel. If the Company operates an ancillary warehouse with a gross floor area of 20,000 square meters or more, or if land development related to the warehouse reaches the threshold set in the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, the Company must file a Prior Environmental Review; a full EIA remains unnecessary unless chemical treatment, dry cleaning or manufacturing processes are later added to the business scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The facility is expected to produce zero industrial process wastewater and no VOCs from routine garment sorting. Any sanitary or incidental discharge must comply with the Water Environment Conservation Act effluent quality limits of BOD 40 mg/L or less, SS 40 mg/L or less, T-N 60 mg/L or less and T-P 8 mg/L or less for discharge to public waters. If refrigeration or HVAC systems are installed in the warehouse, refrigerants must satisfy the Clean Air Conservation Act and ozone-layer protection rules with a preference for HFCs having GWP below 150. Any damaged and unsaleable garments disposed as hazardous or municipal waste must be transported by a licensed waste handler and reported through the Korean Waste Management Integrated System, with manifest quantities recorded for off-site disposal.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a Fire-Fighting System Completion Inspection Certificate from the National Fire Agency or the competent local fire station before stocking the warehouse, and maintain firefighting equipment, evacuation routes and fire safety surveillance under the Firefighting Systems Installation, Maintenance and Safety Control Act. The warehouse must pass the building final inspection under the Building Act, including structural load requirements for racking. If the Company employs five or more workers, it must file a workplace safety report with the Ministry of Employment and Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, appoint a safety and health manager, conduct emergency drills, and adopt a civil defense and fire evacuation plan aligned with Korean disaster-management regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr); export customs clearances administered by Korea Customs Service (KCS) through UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the tax identifier is the Business Registration Number (BRN), which doubles as the Corporate TIN and VAT ID. The entity must complete Commercial Act incorporation before tax filing. The responsible domestic representative submits a Business Registration Application to the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business, via HomeTax or in person. Documents include company certificate or registry extracts, certificate of incorporation and articles of association of any foreign parent (apostilled or notarized with certified Korean translation), board resolution appointing the domestic representative or manager, power of attorney, passport or national ID of the representative, and evidence of the domestic business place such as a lease agreement or office registration. For a non-resident foreign company without a Korean establishment, a domestic tax representative is appointed and the same BRN procedure is completed before the first taxable supply. NTS issues the Certificate of Business Registration; the 10-digit BRN is then activated for electronic tax invoices through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the Yuhan Hoesa is a separate domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act, taxed on worldwide income at entity level; pass-through or transparent treatment is not available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None equivalent to a US check-the-box election. Korean law does not permit a business entity to elect pass-through taxation. A statutory group consolidation election is available for eligible 100% owned domestic subsidiaries under the Corporate Tax Act; OECD/hybrid mismatch anti-avoidance rules under the Act on International Tax Coordination apply to cross-border hybrid instruments and cannot be overcome by an election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None in KRW: any person who starts a business or makes taxable supplies in Korea must register for VAT before business commencement, regardless of turnover. Simplified taxpayer status applies only to low-revenue individual entrepreneurs and does not provide a registration threshold for a corporate Yuhan Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered suppliers must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS e-Tax Invoice system (HomeTax web, EDI, or API) and transmit invoice details to NTS by the day following issuance. There is no pre-issue government clearance or physical tax stamp; the NTS relies on near real-time post-issuance reporting, automated cross-matching against customs export declarations, and continuous anti-fraud validation processing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for the 0% VAT export rate under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act when they are physically exported from the Republic of Korea under a final export customs declaration, and the Korean supplier is the exporter in the customs record. In the off-price apparel liquidation model, the Korean Yuhan Hoesa must have a genuine sale to an offshore buyer, title and risk transfer outside Korea, and a valid export clearance. Qualifying offshore services, not relevant to this apparel scope, are zero-rated if supplied to a nonresident and paid in convertible foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration (final export customs clearance statement) accepted and transmitted in the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical export and showing the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as shipper or consignor and the offshore buyer as consignee or notify party
Export sales contract, purchase order, or equivalent trade documentation evidencing the offshore buyer and sale price

Foreign exchange collection evidence: Export Proceeds Collection Confirmation, remittance receipt, or foreign exchange bank certificate from a Korean foreign exchange bank (Korean equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate or FIRC)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If an exporter cannot substantiate actual export, a genuine offshore buyer, or repatriation of the export proceeds, the NTS will disallow the zero rating, assess VAT at 10% on the supply value, and claw back any refund already paid. The unfaithful return penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes is generally 10% of the unpaid tax, rising to 40% for dishonest or fraudulent returns, plus late-payment interest. Fraudulent export invoices or refund schemes are referred under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act to criminal prosecution. The NTS and KCS retrospectively re-examine prior returns; the national tax collection period may extend to 10 years in cases of fraudulent evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority, with delegated foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act enforced by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized current account convertibility regime under Article 3 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, but residual controls remain for capital account flows and large settlements. Residents and non-resident entities may freely convert KRW for trade and operating expenses, subject to documentary submission to a domestic foreign exchange bank. Export proceeds in foreign currency must be collected through authorized banks; conversion is automatic with no mandatory surrender ratio beyond reporting threshold, yet the receipt must be reported within the statutory deadline. Repatriation of capital, dividends, and liquidation proceeds from a foreign-invested company is generally permitted on a prior-declaration basis, provided the investment was registered with the MOEF under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The Korean won is not fully freely convertible outside Korea; offshore KRW settlement is restricted, and non-resident banks may access KRW only through the FX interbank system. For a wholesale apparel liquidation trading entity, current account convertibility is straightforward, but capital account operations such as capital increase or loan extension require additional declarations to the BOK-MOEF reporting system. The practical hurdle is not convertibility denial but strict evidentiary documentation and timeline compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Korea abolished mandatory surrender of export proceeds; however, every export contract exceeding USD 50,000 must be reported to a designated foreign exchange bank within the relevant transaction period, and export receipts must be received into a domestic foreign exchange account within 90 days from the date of export, with extensions available for trade credit periods not exceeding 180 days.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Trade Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Trade Settlement Account and FX Hedging Facility Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMI solutions such as Wise, Airwallex, and Currenxie are not recognized as licensed deposit-taking institutions in South Korea. The Korean banking law reserves current account deposit-taking and KRW FX settlement to licensed banks and specialized mutual institutions. EMIs may only provide non-account payment initiation or remittance facilitation if partnered with a domestic tier-1 bank, and even then, they cannot open KRW-denominated settlement accounts for an onshore entity directly. For a Korean LLC engaged in apparel off-price wholesale, relying on an EMI would create non-compliance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act because export collections must be routed through a Korean foreign exchange bank or its directly corresponding overseas branch. Feasibility is therefore low as a standalone banking rail; EMIs are viable solely as ancillary payment trigger tools after primary treasury accounts are established. Legal constraints require the underlying Korean entity to maintain at least one domestic bank account for statutory reporting and tax verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean anti-money laundering regulations and the Financial Transactions Reports Act mandate that a corporate account opening require the physical presence of the statutory director or an duly authorized attorney-in-fact at the bank branch to execute the client due diligence process. In practice, most nationwide banks require the representative director to appear in person for first account activation; remote consular proxy opening is not universally accepted. Some banks allow video-call KYC for the initial interview if the director is physically abroad, but all original corporate seal certificates, apostilled board resolutions, and passport copies must be delivered by courier and verified by a designated Korean notary or consulate. Practical recommendation is in-person branch onboarding with two-day reservation, followed by electronic banking activation after the account is opened.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity detailing a foreign-parent LLC with no clear natural person controlling the Korean subsidiary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified registrar diagram showing the full ownership chain, corporate registry extracts from the home country, apostilled IDs of the ultimate beneficial owner and Korean director, and a board resolution confirming authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transnational sourcing of overstock branded garments creating high counterparty anonymity, inconsistent invoice pricing, and potential grey-market licensing triggers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed brand-authorized liquidation agreements, original manufacturer invoices, certificate of authenticity per shipment, loyalty vendor compliance records, and audited inventory reconciliation to prove purchase from licensed liquidators rather than unauthorized secondary channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated wire thresholds for trade revenue crossing from multiple offshore marketplaces into one Korean account, possibly signaling third-party collection arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed marketplace seller agreements, merchant of record contracts, customer collections flow chart, export bills of lading, and quarterly projected export revenue forecast to evidence that each remittance is derived from real apparel wholesale transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Headers mismatch in the FX settlement instructions between Korean entity name, foreign trade counterpart bank, and payment swift BIC of the liquidation buyers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original documentary collection and letter-of-credit files, purchase order swifts, bank guarantee evidence, invoice packing list cross-matching, and a written counterparty nexus intention letter authenticated by both treasury officers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment from a non-resident shareholder into the Korean LLC must be filed with the MOEF under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, then routed through an internationally authorized bank using wire protocol SWIFT MT103 with standard purpose of claim code F and Korea-required FDI narrative. The bank will issue a certificate of capital importation before the amount is credited to a temporary capital escrow account; after the Capital Verification Report is issued by the authorized bank, the funds can be transferred to the operating account. If the share capital is contributed as a bank loan, the borrower must file a loan agreement with the BOK/MOEF system within 30 days and secure an inward loan registration certificate. All payments must be made in convertible foreign currency; KRW remittances from an overseas-incorporated account are only accepted for investment if the sender holds a MOEF-issued KRW settlement permission. The Korean repatriated treasury account must be classified under foreign exchange purpose code 3011 for equity capital and 3021 for long-term loans.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for buying off-price apparel from foreign suppliers should use SWIFT MT103 direct wire for amounts below USD 100,000, with purpose of remittance code A100-FX for trade payments and supporting import declarations submitted via the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS. Larger settlements should follow documentary collection DP/DA through the trading bank or commercial letters of credit where the Korean importer opens an irrevocable LC, in which case the full LC text must be forwarded to the overseas advising bank and the bill of lading must be endorsed to order. The settlement window should be synchronized with the BOK/NBVS statement cycle to avoid late declaration penalties. For payments to suppliers in heavily controlled countries, extra compliance due diligence and potentially a restricted country license from the MOEF Financial Supervisory Service must be obtained before any MT103 release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, available only for underlying trade exposure backed by invoices, bills of lading, or import/export contracts, with tenors typically up to 12 months and rollover requiring revised exposure proof.

Non-deliverable forwards on USD/KRW traded offshore through non-resident counterparties, permissible for hedging KRW receivables/payables where settlement is in USD; must be reported to the BOK when notional exposure exceeds USD 1 million per counterparty.

Currency swaps with a domestic bank where the Korean entity exchanges KRW operational surplus for USD to fund future trade disbursement, subject to a genuine trade-finance covenant and mandatory inclusion in quarterly FX exposure reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and year-end closing financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, and tax adjustment schedules) for the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following a December 31 fiscal year end; if the fiscal year ends on another date, within 3 months of that fiscal year end. An extension of up to 4 months may be granted with prior NTS approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Negligence tax: 20% of unpaid corporate tax for unintentional failure to file and 40% for intentional non-filing; understatement or overclaim penalty: 10% of the understated tax amount or overstated refund; overdue interest: 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum) from the day after the statutory due date; prolonged delinquency triggers NTS asset seizure, bank freezes, cancellation of business registration, and departure restriction against the representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surtax return and payment for corporate income tax (local corporate income surtax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal local government (si/gun/gu) where the registered office is located, filed via the Wetax e-government system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following the fiscal year end, same as the national corporate income tax deadline; for a non-December fiscal year end, within 3 months of the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local delinquency penalties: 20% negligence tax on unpaid local income tax for unfiled returns, 10% for underreported amounts, and overdue interest of 0.022% per day; local government may seize bank accounts, real estate, and receivables and may ultimately revoke the business registration for chronic non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax (VAT) return and payment for the first and second semi-annual tax periods, including advance VAT prepayment returns where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First-half period (January 1 to June 30): due by July 25; second-half period (July 1 to December 31): due by January 25 of the following year; quarterly prepayment returns for enterprises with annual VAT payable exceeding KRW 300 million: due by April 25 and October 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT negligence tax: 10% of unpaid VAT for non-filing, 20% for inaccurate or unfaithful filing, and 0.022% daily interest on late payment; repeated failure to file VAT may lead to business registration closure/cancellation and criminal referral in aggravated cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements by members and, if statutory audit applies, the independent auditor's report; audited financial statements must be retained and, when required by the NTS, submitted together with the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members' meeting internally; tax records retained for National Tax Service (NTS) inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved by the members' meeting within 6 months of the fiscal year end; audited financial statements must be prepared and delivered to members within 2 weeks before the annual members' meeting and filed with the NTS by March 31 as part of the corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve or retain financial statements is an irregularity under the Korean Commercial Act and may result in fines not exceeding KRW 20 million for directors for failure to prepare or maintain statutory books; for externally audited companies, failure to prepare or submit audited financial statements can trigger corrective orders, administrative fines, and a deficiency disposition under the External Audit Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment change report for any transfer of equity interests, capital increase/decrease, amendment of articles, or relocation of head office of the foreign-invested enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA foreign investment support center or designated foreign exchange banks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the date of any change in the foreign investor's equity interest, paid-in capital, decision to invest, or company attributes under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 2 million (approximately USD 1,500) for failure to file the change report; false reporting can result in criminal fines and loss of foreign-investment protections and tax benefits under relevant special laws.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, etc., a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) is subject to mandatory independent CPA audit if its total assets at the end of the relevant fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million at 1,300 KRW/USD). No purely turnover-based or headcount-based audit trigger exists under Korean law for an ordinary private limited liability company; the balance-sheet asset test is the primary quantitative threshold. Additional mandatory audit is required for listed stock companies, public-interest entities designated by the Financial Services Commission, and certain large business group affiliates regardless of legal form. A small off-price wholesale apparel LLC with total assets below KRW 12 billion is not statutorily required to obtain an external audit, but a certified audit may be required by lenders, investors, or contractual commitments.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board for publicly accountable and externally audited companies; Korean GAAP for non-public corporations not electing K-IFRS; and the Korean Accounting Standards for SMEs for small and medium entities with total assets below KRW 12 billion and no statutory external audit obligation. Financial statements must be prepared in Korean and, if audited, accompanied by an independent CPA auditor's report issued under the Korean external audit law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public UBO filing register for private limited liability companies. Beneficial ownership information is confirmed through the annual corporate income tax return and, if the company is a foreign-invested enterprise, through the change reports required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Any transfer of shares or equity interests must be recorded in the company's register of members and transfer register; a foreign investor transfer must be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of the transfer. Korean financial institutions will collect and refresh beneficial ownership data for AML compliance in connection with the corporate bank relationship, but there is no standalone annual UBO filing to a corporate registry for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 2,500 per year for outsourced registered office and corporate secretarial services in Seoul; no statutory Korean registered agent requirement exists for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 35,000 per year for a mandatory or voluntary certified audit of a small wholesale apparel trading company, depending on transaction volume, inventory scope, number of bank relationships, and the selected CPA firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surcharge yielding aggregate 26.4% effective top marginal burden
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday exists. Select preferential deductions apply: 5%-15% R&D tax credit, 3%-10% facility investment credit, and special tax reduction zones (Free Economic Zones) for high-tech foreign direct investment subject to capital investment thresholds; unused credits carry forward within statutory limits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (Foreign Corporation), filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr); attached annexes including financial statements, reconciliation schedules, international transaction report, and transfer pricing documentation schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return plus semi-annual interim prepayments; the interim return is filed within 3 months after the first six months of the fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final corporate income tax return is due within 3 months from the last day of the fiscal year. For calendar-year entities, the statutory deadline is March 31; electronically filed returns benefit from an administrative 1-month extension to April 30

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification and business registration number; entity legal form code and fiscal year dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Foreign Investment Company Registration Number and the tax office jurisdiction code for the Korean branch or DTA-claimed residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of total revenue, gross profit, and off-price liquidation sales recognized under the accrual method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Korean-source gross sales only; attach reconciliation of worldwide purchase price components and landed cost under the tax code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions, including cost of sales, distribution costs, personnel expenses, depreciation, and bad debt write-offs consistent with the corporate income tax art. 19 list of losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign headquarter allocations are deductible only to the extent supported by economic substance documentation and arm-length charge agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryforward, tax-free reserves, and treaty-recognized permanent establishment adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the DTA attributes profits to a Korean fixed base of off-price wholesale operation, recognize only those profits; attach Form Certified Statement of Residence (TRC) and treaty position memo.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate tax at progressive brackets, local income surtax, specified additional taxes, and credits such as foreign tax credit and investment tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxes at bracket rates from KRW 0 to 300 billion; apply treaty withholding credit and the domestic CFC rule adjustments if remitted profits are retained offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable, interim prepayment credits, withholding credits, and balance due or refund claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign corporation has no permanent establishment and received only dividend interest or royalty income, record final withheld tax in Box 88 and submit the withholding certification from the Korean payor.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or unfaithful filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax (40% if the report is fraudulent or willfully omitted) plus daily late payment surcharge of 0.025% of the underpaid amount; failure to file the interim return triggers a 10% negligence penalty. A failure to attach transfer pricing documentation attracts an administrative fine up to KRW 5 million plus penalty tax adjustments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national source tax on gross dividends plus 2% local income tax surcharge, aggregate 22% for non-resident shareholders without treaty coverage
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA reduction, the non-resident beneficiary must obtain a Certificate of Residency (TRC) from the competent authority of the residence jurisdiction and provide it to the Korean payor before the payment date. The payor submits an Application for Tax Treaty Withholding Reduction/Exemption to the NTS branch having jurisdiction over the payor. The application must include the treaty article citation, beneficial ownership declaration, and complete ownership and holding period evidence for dividend rate eligibility. If treaty relief is not applied at source, the beneficiary may claim a refund through the annual corporate/individual return or by separate tax refund application within three years from the tax year-end.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic rates for royalties and interest are 20% national plus 2% local income surcharge (aggregate 22%). Under the OECD/MLI-based Korean DTAs, interest is typically reduced to 10%-15%, royalties to 5%-15%, and equipment rental royalties to 0%-10%, subject to beneficial ownership and the principal purpose test introduced by the Multilateral Convention.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion in the taxable year simultaneously require submission of Master File and Local File with the annual corporate return; an International Transaction Report (annex to the CIT return) is mandatory for aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 500 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not have the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the substance-over-form doctrine under the Framework Act on National Taxes and OECD BEPS directives apply. Korean tax authorities deny treaty benefits where an off-price liquidator is established as a conduit without real resale, inventory custody, pricing, order, or staff function; this is reinforced by the Multilateral Instrument’s Principal Purpose Test incorporated into Korea’s DTAs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally underreporting liquidation proceeds, creating fictitious purchase invoices for surplus garment stock, or converting cash from auction sales into unreported owner disbursements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fraudulent underreporting penalty of 40% of the evaded corporate tax, dishonesty penalty of 20%, daily late payment interest of 0.025%, plus collection seizure and freezing of bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the Punishment Act for Tax Offenses, Art. 3, responsible directors face imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to three times the evaded tax. Civil personal liability attaches where directors structured the concealment, and the NTS may obtain travel bans and asset preservation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing / Base Erosion Shell Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an undercapitalized Korean Yuhan Hoesa with foreign related-party purchasing at excessive margins, no identifiable distribution activity, or no stocking and pricing authority, thereby creating synthetic tax losses and shifting profit to a tax-haven trading shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korean tax office re-determines the arm's-length margin, disallows the intercompany invoices, imposes additional corporate tax up to 24%, adds a 20% negligence penalty, and asserts foreign withholding tax on imputed dividends or branch remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly establish an economic-substance-free structure are jointly liable for the assessed deficiencies, may be subject to investigation for violation of the International Tax Adjustment Act, and face imprisonment up to 3 years where deliberate false transfer pricing documentation is used to conceal tax avoidance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving unexplainable wire transfers into domestic bank accounts without mandatory suspicious transaction reporting, splitting cross-border settlement payments to evade the KRW 20 million reporting threshold, or using nominee accounts for liquidation merchants under the Financial Transactions Reports Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to report or providing false information triggers imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to KRW 500 million; the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit can order account seizure, criminal confiscation of proceeds, and permanent revocation of banking licenses for collaborating institutions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate officers who order or permit the circumvention of the AML reporting mandate are personally criminally liable, face exit controls, and are subject to civil forfeiture of all illicit enrichment derived from the unreported remittance flows.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or royalties to a non-resident parent without deducting Korean withholding tax, or claiming a DTA reduced rate without a valid TRC, beneficial ownership evidence, or with the main purpose of treaty-shopping the off-price garment liquidation profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean withholding agent is held jointly liable for the unpaid WHT, a 10% negligence penalty, daily 0.025% overdue interest, and denial of the treaty rate if the principal purpose test is violated. The Korean payor entity is also liable for the grossed-up reimbursement amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false withholding certificates or who misuse a DTA while knowing the foreign recipient lacks economic substance incur personal civil restitution to the tax office; under the Punishment Act for Tax Offenses, they may be sentenced to imprisonment up to 3 years, and a travel ban is automatically applied during prosecution.
